intro: Five long reads people saved with Xtracticle this week — Harrison Chase on giving agents real company knowledge, a sober look at six weeks of falling AI stocks, a copywriter’s framework for ads to cold audiences, a plain-language primer on automating tasks with Grok Bot, and a solo route to shipping a 3D WeChat mini game with AI.

items.author: Harrison Chase
items.title: How to build a knowledge factory
items.summary: LangChain’s Harrison Chase argues that agents fail at work for lack of company knowledge rather than better models, and describes a “knowledge factory” that collects, curates and updates what experienced staff know so agents can use it.

items.author: The Kobeissi Letter
items.title: -$6 Trillion In 45 Days: Is This A "Bubble" Or An Opportunity?
items.summary: The Kobeissi Letter walks through the six weeks since the S&P 500’s last record, from AI spending worries to rate and election news, to ask whether the slide in AI stocks is a burst bubble or a buying opportunity.

items.author: Derick Carneiro
items.title: how I write ads that make strangers buy
items.summary: A young direct-response copywriter explains why ads to people who have never heard of a brand should lead with attention and a new idea rather than price or offer, and breaks the job of such an ad into four smaller sales.

items.author: lauren
items.title: Automate Anything with Grok Bot
items.summary: A plain-language introduction to automation as a goal plus a process, with everyday examples, and how to break a task into steps that Grok Bot can then carry out for you.

items.author: Fini.Yang
items.title: 不用等版号！一个人靠 AI 搓出 3D 小游戏直接过审上线，从建游到接广告赚钱的全套开源工具全公开
items.summary: A step-by-step account of building a 3D WeChat mini game alone with AI agents and an open-source plugin, fixing the black screens and size limits that break such games on phones, and getting it through review with ad revenue switched on.
